fees.conditions: Fee schedule (2026-11-02): 'Virtual card issuance fee' 0 for both card types. Virtual card only — the ATM row reads 'Not applicable to virtual cards'; no physical card is mentioned on any page read.
Fee schedule (2026-11-02): 'Annual fee' 0, 'Inactivity fee' 0, 'Termination fee' 0 for both card types.

Fee schedule (2026-11-02), Global Card: 'Foreign exchange fee' = 'Visa exchange rate + 0% markup'. Press release (2026-08-31): 'Other than foreign exchange fees that Visa may charge for certain currencies under its rules, MEXC applies no additional exchange-rate markup.' The 1% transaction fee (see 'other') applies to every purchase, foreign or not.
No ATM function: fee schedule row 'ATM withdrawal fee' reads 'Not applicable to virtual cards' for both card types. Cash withdrawal is therefore not available (limit modelled as 0).

Fee schedule (2026-11-02): 'Top-up fee' 0 (no top-up limits stated). Funding is in USDT via the MEXC Fiat account ('Transfer USDT to your Fiat account … then add funds to your card' — product page FAQ). Network/deposit fees to bring USDT onto MEXC are not part of the card schedule.
Fee schedule (2026-11-02): 'Crypto conversion fee' 0% for both card types — defined as the fee applied 'when crypto assets in your account are converted into fiat currency to complete a purchase'.

Global Card 'Transaction fee' 1% of the purchase value on EVERY purchase (fee schedule 2026-11-02; example: 100 USD purchase → 1 USD fee, 101 USDT debited). Also: refund fee 1%; failed-transaction fee 0 USD if the failed-transaction rate is < 20%, 0.5 USD per transaction if ≥ 20%; small-amount transaction fee 0.1 USD for purchases under 1 USD. 'Fee rates may be adjusted during the event' (no event described). The launch promotion '0 fees' on all purchases ran 'from launch through September 30, 2026' (press release) and has expired; the press release said rates would then 'start from as low as 1%'.

Credited in USDT to the Fiat account within T+3 calendar days of settlement; the monthly cap is shared across all MEXC Cards of the same user and resets at 00:00 UTC+8 on the 1st; excluded: certain merchant categories (separate article, not read), forced-authorization and risk-flagged transactions; cashback is clawed back on refunds. Unreadable this run: 'How to Apply for the MEXC Global Card' and 'How to Apply for MEXC Card (APAC)' support guides (client-rendered shells — countries, KYC documents), the Learn articles 'What Is the MEXC Global Card…' and 'MEXC Card: Supported Countries, Restricted Regions & What KYC Actually Requires' (client error on mexc.com and mexc.co), the M-Score/VVIP page (fetcher provenance), the MCC exclusion list and the APAC Rewards FAQ. An older Learn page about a 'virtual MEXC MasterCard' (EEA list, 1% top-up, inner test users) was read but describes a different, earlier product and is not used as evidence.

editorial.summary: Virtual Visa card from the MEXC exchange, in two versions with separate fee schedules: the MEXC Global Card (1% fee on every purchase, Visa FX rate with 0% markup) and the MEXC Card (APAC) (0% purchase fee, Visa rate + 1% cross-border fee). No issuance, annual, top-up or conversion fee; no ATM function. Funded in USDT from the MEXC Fiat account, converted at spend. Cashback in USDT follows the user's VVIP level: 4% (cap 50 USDT/month) at Standard, 6% (150) at Premier, 10% (800) at Elite — the M-Score thresholds behind the levels are not published on the pages read. Issuer not disclosed; no country list published; MEXC account KYC ('advanced') required.
good_for: MEXC users in a supported region who want a virtual Visa with Apple Pay / Google Pay funded directly from their USDT balance
Small monthly budgets: the 4% Standard cashback is capped at 50 USDT, i.e. it is maxed out at 1,250 USDT of eligible spend
not_for: Anyone who needs cash: no ATM function on either version
Residents of countries not confirmed as supported — no official list could be read
Users expecting the 'up to 10%' headline: Elite requires an undisclosed M-Score; the 1% Global Card transaction fee eats a quarter of the 4% base cashback
watch_outs: Global Card: 1% transaction fee on every purchase since the launch promotion ended on 2026-09-30; the APAC version charges 0% but adds 1% on non-USD purchases.
Issuer and programme manager are not named anywhere: 'The Card program is operated by third-party service providers.'
Cashback level and cap 'subject to the information displayed in the app', shared across all of a user's MEXC Cards, clawed back on refunds (an 'outstanding amount' can be created).
Earn rate contradiction: press release 'up to 7%' vs product page '3% APR'.
Refund fee 1% (3% for non-USD refunds on the APAC card); 0.1 USD fee on Global Card purchases under 1 USD; failed-transaction fee if the decline rate reaches 20%.
Supported-countries and KYC pages are client-rendered and could not be read — eligibility is unverified.
